title: Methodological considerations for the force-matching task
evidence_type: peer-reviewed primary single-session laboratory methodological analysis; published aggregates only
design: Four targets x eight repetitions x two counterbalanced32-trial condition blocks; one session, randomized target order. No retest.
precision: No split-half coefficient CIs or cross-window/condition covariance extracted. New arithmetic is descriptive, not significant/equivalent claim.
negative_findings: Little overall64-trial mean trend and nonsignificant replication-count comparisons preserved; do not relabel as absence of condition-specific learning.
limitations: Split-half is not retest, difference-score reliability or latent-factor reliability
Counterbalanced pooled slope does not isolate indirect learning
Device-specific timing and possible slider lag
Nested repetitions are not independent sessions
Selected aggregate table/narrative summaries differ and are not silently reconciled
No TS, severe persistent adult, functional-outcome or treatment validation
cohort_overlap: Paper notes smaller sample already reported in McNaughton2021; do not count as independent replication.
funding_conflicts: Chiropractic Australia PhD scholarship; portion commissioned device construction; authors declare no conflicts.
adverse_events: Not a treatment study; no clinical safety estimate.
claim_supported: Same-session group means may be similar with fewer repetitions while split-half precision and condition contrast depend on protocol.
claim_not_supported: Validated repeat-session Tourette biomarker, condition-specific learning absent, causal mechanism or treatment benefit.
access: Lawful EuropePMC CC BY4.0 full manuscript inspected, no raw dataset opened, only original summary and aggregate inputs retained.
correction_retraction_check: Exact DOI web query found no verified notice; bounded.
next_verification_task: Close window/split-half audit. Require lawful aggregate same-task repeat-session coefficient+CI, absolute agreement, interval/practice/order/calibration and exact endpoint; no repeated null search or participant-data access.
